title: Robert R. Livingston to John Jay, Philadelphia, 28 Nov 1781: the 'addition to your cypher' line (catalogue 636)

documents.shelfmark: NHi Jay Papers (EJ 598), ALS; photostat in Columbia Jay Papers ldpd:6328, p. 7

plaintext.source: Livingston's draft (NHi R. R. Livingston Papers, EJ 1537; Columbia ldpd:11572 p. 3) glosses each pair; Jay's copy of the Thomson code (Columbia ldpd:50144 p. 2) lists be-he against 600-605; 'to your cypher' interlined on the ALS.

transcription.source: Columbia DLC IIIF, full-resolution tiles stitched (about 2200x2900 px)
transcription.notes: One line at the foot of the ALS; the draft's glosses De and Fe are smudged.

system.summary: Charles Thomson's printed 600-entry syllable-and-word nomenclator (WE007 family), in a copy numbered differently from Jay's; the line adds six new groups 600-605 for be, ce, de, fe, ge, he, each defined by spelling it in two existing groups.
system.sibling_key: Jay's copy of the same printed form (WE007), numbered differently
system.notes: Lost-code values given by the line: b 69, c 538, d 346, e 226, f 216, g 209, h 259, to 398, your 264, cypher 23.473.370.

prior_solution.where: Glosses under each pair in Livingston's draft (NHi) and the entries be-he 600-605 on Jay's key sheet (NNC); the modern edition (Selected Papers of John Jay 2, n. 7) calls the line undecipherable.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue (pasted solve-page brief).

solution.what: Read Founders Jay/01-02-02-0272 and the editorial note on Jay's codes; the 'passage' is the last line, groups 600-605 added to the cipher, printed as figures.
Stitched Jay's copy of the Thomson code (Columbia ldpd:50144) from IIIF tiles.
Found handwritten entries be 600, ce 601, de 602, fe 603, ge 604, he 605 on p. 2 of Jay's key sheet.
Looked the addition's numbers up in WE007 (Jay's copy): twelve, into, el, en, sha, their + edge; not WE007.
Tested ldpd:50124, catalogued as the key to this letter: a one-part word code (69 apparent, 226 destroy); not this key.
19th-c. copy of the 20 Oct 1781 coded passage with figures under the words (ldpd:32488): not 203, will 175, his 139, for 235 in the lost code, unlike WE007; same form, renumbered.
Stitched the six Columbia records of the 28 Nov letter (ALS, draft, duplicate, triplicate, photostats).
Draft (ldpd:11572 p. 3) glosses the six pairs Be, Ce, De, Fe, Ge, he; ALS interlines 'to your cypher' over 398 264 23.473.370.
Transcribed the ALS addition line, 17 cipher tokens.
Draft glosses and Jay's key sheet agree pair for pair; the printed Thomson form lacks bare be/ce/de/fe/ge/he but has ar/er/ir/or/ur, against the edition's r-syllable reading.

outcome.method_basis: Livingston's draft glosses each pair of the line and Jay's key sheet lists the same six syllables against 600-605; the ALS line was transcribed and checked against both.
outcome.notes: The edition's 'syllables ending in r' is wrong: 226 is e.

credits.note: Glosses in Livingston's draft and the be-he entries on Jay's copy of the Thomson code

independent reading of the addition line the same day, by another route: the ALS (lost Palfrey numbering) aligned word by word on the triplicate (Thomson code, key kept) gives 226 = e, 69 = b, 346 = d, 398 = to from the letter's own text, hence be 600, ce 601, de 602, fe 603, ge 604, he 605 (c, f, g, h by order and by Livingston's entries on Jay's key sheet); also found that 226 is e, not r. This project's reading (draft glosses) is the same and has priority

texts.label: Livingston to Jay, Philadelphia, 28 Nov 1781, last line (NHi Jay Papers EJ 598)
texts.summary: Livingston tells Jay to add six groups to his cipher: be 600, ce 601, de 602, fe 603, ge 604, he 605. Each is defined by spelling the syllable in two existing groups, the second always e (226).

reading_review.note: One instruction line; reads as a sentence: Make this addition to your cypher: be 600, ce 601, de 602, fe 603, ge 604, he 605.
